abilities.name: Cultivate plants
abilities.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-prepared soil plot, where it may establish as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect plots or plant sources; end unfinished planting.
abilities.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1) gathered from a living plant; x, y a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, with fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Two paid rounds of 1.5 energy: prepare the site, then transfer the unit; the action continues itself, and plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect: target a plot or plant source in reach; one round, 0.2 energy (baseline probe observation). End: stops unfinished planting; one round, no energy. Tend is refused at no cost: no water, fertilizer or other treatment exists yet. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is provided.
abilities.effects: Preparing keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Transfer moves it, with origin and age, into the plot, where it cannot be eaten or used; the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one. It gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season, so cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On establishing, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock and a ceiling of at most 4, regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone through gather; nothing is copied or guaranteed. Inspect records only visible stage, stock, soil and weather as an unverified personal record. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. End, or death, before transfer returns the unit once (where the person died); a transferred unit stays planted. No reward or refund.

execution.progress: Two paid one-round stages whose job, reserved unit and plot persist across interruption; resuming pays only the remaining stage after revalidation; completion, failure, ending and death settle once. Growth proceeds only in ordinary simulation.

abilities.name: Construct a branch screen
abilities.function: Assess a site and test a post, then build a small porous woven branch windbreak (no roof) beside a resting place; inspect, repair, dismantle or cancel.
abilities.costs: Study: 4 rounds. One branch unit is one piece; a screen takes 11 (3 uprights, 8 rods). assess (x, y, orientation; within reach): 1 round, 0.2 energy; checks a clear 1.2 x 0.6 m footprint of ordinary dry soil and the lee floor. assess with post (owned branch unit): post trial at x, y; 1 round, 0.5 energy. assemble (x, y, orientation, materials: exactly 11 owned untreated or sound recovered branch units) needs your passing trial in the footprint; 8 paid rounds of 1.5 energy (2 seat uprights, 4 weave rods, 1 align, 1 stability check), continuing each round; with target it resumes. repair (builder; target, components: installed piece ids, materials: as many units): 1.5 energy per round, one removal and one fitting round per piece, then a check round; components [] only rechecks. inspect (target in reach): 1 round, 0.2 energy. dismantle (builder): 1 round and 1 energy per 3 pieces. cancel: no energy.
abilities.effects: Units stay carried and owned until a paid round installs them with origin and age; nothing is created or used up. A trial on ordinary soil (waterlogging at most 0.1, no hazard) seats the post 0.25 m and you keep it; elsewhere it fails; a post below condition 0.5 breaks into damaged material. The check passes only if every piece has condition at least 0.5 and the uprights stand in such soil; else the screen is unstable. World wind has no direction; the exposure law takes it as coming from +x (orientation 0 faces it). A complete screen removes min(0.35, solid share of sound pieces, about 0.36) x facing of the wind part of the outdoor chill for a body wholly on the 0.9 x 0.9 m lee floor 0.45-1.35 m behind it; never rain chill or air temperature; none in wind above 0.8 or with another shelter. Wear per round 0.0005 + 0.002 x (rain + wind); a loose rod opens a gap, a loose upright ends the effect until repair. Removed pieces lie at the site. Unworked rounds, low energy, leaving reach, wet ground or a person on the footprint pause at no charge. Cancel or death returns uninstalled units once. No reward or refund.

execution.progress: Paid one-round stages that persist across interruption; resuming pays only the next stage after rechecks. Other modes take one round.

abilities.name: Hand-weave a fiber mat
abilities.function: Test a 0.1 sample of owned fiber, then hand-plait 4 units into one portable 0.45 x 0.45 m sitting mat; inspect, sit on, repair, lift, place, dismantle or cancel.
abilities.costs: Study: 3 rounds. A unit is one world unit of fiber (dry grass: 0.1 mass). test (sample: owned stack): 1 round, 0.5 energy. assemble (x, y: a 0.45 m square in reach on land, clear of plants, objects and other people; materials: exactly 4 owned units of one fiber from sources your passing test covers): a 0.5-energy layout round, then 6 paid rounds of 1 energy (2 strip-forming, 3 interlacing and edge-tucking, 1 lift check), continuing each round; with target it resumes. inspect (target in reach): 1 round, 0.2. trial (stand on a complete mat on firm ground, waterlogging at most 0.1, no rain, nobody else on it): 1 round, 0.2. Maker only: repair (target inspected since its last check; materials: 1 unit of its fiber): 3 rounds of 1 energy (remove broken stems, interlace, lift check); lift, or place (carried mat; x, y as for assemble): 1 round, 0.2; dismantle: 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none.
abilities.effects: A test passes only for thin stems (dry grass, reeds) with flexibility at least 0.4 and an intact untreated sample, which stays as owned tested scrap; stem length and moisture are not represented. The layout needs 0.3645 mass of intact fiber (two crossing layers of 0.6 per m2, x1.5 for overlaps and tucked edges); less is a measured shortfall that returns all fiber. Strip rounds move the fiber into the work. The lift check keeps the needed tenths (dry grass 3.7), returns the rest as owned offcuts or scraps, and passes with full fiber and condition at least 0.5 (largest opening 0.06 x (1 - condition) m); else the mat stays failed. Condition (intact share) falls 0.0005 per round, 0.002 with a person on the mat; below 0.5 it needs repair and a new trial. Repair turns up to 1 unit of broken stems into scrap and refills with new fiber. Dismantle returns intact fiber and scraps. A carried mat is reserved owned fiber and counts as load. Trials record hold, slip and loose stems only; no comfort, warmth, rain, wind or rest effect. Unworked rounds, low energy, leaving reach or a person on the square pause at no charge; cancel or death returns unused fiber once and leaves the work. Nothing is refunded.

abilities.name: Hand-break food
abilities.function: Apply bounded bare-hand bending force once to each selected whole unit of owned food: trial one unit or prepare several. The actual material decides whether it snaps into coarse pieces, deforms or resists. Inspect or cancel the work.
abilities.costs: Study: 2 rounds at 0.2 energy. inputStackId: the exact id of an owned, unreserved, untreated, unspoiled food item your own record shows as edible; resource names are not accepted. trial: quantity 1; 1 round, 1 energy. prepare: quantity 1-10 whole units of that item, all reserved at once; 1 round and 1 energy per unit, continuing each round; resume with prepare and workId. inspect (workId, or inputStackId of your item): 1 round, 0.2 energy. cancel (optional workId): 1 round, no energy. Too little energy for the next unit or a round not worked pauses before any charge; refused requests spend nothing. No tool, support, water, heat or vessel is used or provided.
abilities.effects: Each paid unit gets one two-hand bending attempt while held. Rigid, inflexible tissue small enough for hand force snaps into one lot of 2 coarse pieces; soft or flexible tissue deforms without separating; harder or larger units resist and stay whole and unchanged. Each worked unit becomes its own owned lot of the same food and quantity with the same origin, harvest time, decay, nutrition and toxicity; nothing detaches and pieces add no food. Results are raw food eaten with eat under the ordinary rules: shape alone changes no nutrition, safety, keeping, taste or meal variety. No washing, peeling, cooking, detoxifying or preservation; food keeps ageing, also while paused. Each worked unit records its observed response as a verified personal record; a repeated response confirms nothing new. Broken or deformed lots cannot be worked again in this version. Cancel returns unworked units once, unchanged; worked lots stay. Death leaves unworked units where the person died; spoiled reserved units are not replaced. Paid effort is never refunded; no reward or mastery is granted.

execution.progress: One paid unit per round; the exact work, reserved units and worked lots persist across interruption, and resuming by workId pays only the next unit after rechecks. Trial, inspect and cancel take one round.

abilities.name: Hand-twist fiber cord
abilities.function: Sample owned fiber, hand-twist a two-ply cord up to 0.30 m in four paid rounds, inspect it, load-trial it between both hands, or cancel; actual material and geometry decide results.
abilities.costs: Study: 3 rounds at 0.2 energy. materials: [{stackId: exact owned unreserved item id, quantity in 0.1 steps}]. sample: one non-food item, 0.1; 1 round, 0.5 energy. make (materials: 0.2-1 unit of one fiber and source, each covered by your passing sample of its source and processing at most 0.05 above its condition; requestedLength m): reserves it, then 4 paid rounds of 1 energy (separate-align, twist, counter-ply, release-check), continuing each round; resume with make and workId only. inspect (targetId: your item from this work, or workId): 1 round, 0.2. trial (targetId: your cord or fragment of at least 0.2 unit and 0.12 m; trialForce N; trialDuration s): 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none. Work needs dry footing and nobody within your radius plus half the cord. Unworked rounds or low energy pause uncharged; refusals and irrelevant arguments spend nothing; nothing is refunded.
abilities.effects: Only thin stems separate; only reed has a strand law (existing reed law: 1.8 m stems, 500 kg/m3, 8 MPa x (1 - 0.55 x water share 0.9), creep 0.003); dry grass reports the gap. A sample is split, bent, twisted and pulled at 5 N, kept as a tested lot or cracked scrap, and reports only separation, retained twist, fractures and force. Make round 1 sets broken strands aside as scrap and derives the cord from conserved volume: two plies, each half the solid volume over length x 1.155 twist take-up + 0.02 m loose ends; plies of 1-12 mm and strands no shorter than a ply, else a measured shortfall returns the fiber. The release check needs condition 0.5 and gives an owned untested cord. Trial force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, grip 10000 N/m x cord width); breaking force = 2 x ply area x wet strength x 0.75 x condition. It records grip slip, extension and creep; load above half the breaking force breaks that share of strands; a break leaves two owned fragments. Worked fiber loses 0.0005 condition per round. A pass means only that force for that time. Cancel or death releases unworked fiber once and leaves the workpiece. No reward or strength rating.

abilities.name: Hand-tie cord knot
abilities.function: Tie an overhand knot in your own finished fiber cord with bare hands in three paid rounds, inspect it, load-trial it by its two tails, untie it, or cancel; the actual cord and its material decide results.
abilities.costs: Study: 3 rounds at 0.2 energy. targetId: exact id of your own unreserved cord or cord fragment from hand-twist-fiber-cord. attempt (knot: overhand): reserves the cord, then 3 paid rounds of 0.5 energy (lay-bend-loop, pass-end-through, dress-release-check), continuing each round; a loose undressed knot needs only the last; resume with attempt and workId only. inspect (targetId or workId): 1 round, 0.2. trial (a tied knot; trialForce N above 0 to 10; trialDuration s above 0 to 60): 1 round, 0.5. untie (a knot): 2 paid rounds of 0.5 (draw-end-back, open-loop). cancel: none. Work needs dry footing and nobody within your radius plus half the cord. Unworked rounds or low energy pause uncharged; refusals and irrelevant arguments spend nothing; nothing is refunded.
abilities.effects: Law cord-knot@1 on the same item: width = 2 ply diameters; the centreline (overall length) is conserved as two tails plus the knot path. Lobes bend no tighter than one width nor than the bend limit of the cord's material, which the first round measures; the knot path is 3 pi x lobe radius + width, centred. A loop needs a 0.02 m opening and each hand a 0.02 m pinch: a loop leaving too little end, or an end too short to pass and pinch, ends that paid stage. Dressing seats the lobes; a tail shorter than 0.02 m + width slips out on release, else the knot is tied. Trial: a 0.05 m grip per tail kept 0.01 m clear of the knot; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x width); knotted breaking force = fiber-cord breaking force / (1 + width / (2 x lobe radius)); it records extension, creep, strand damage above half that force, or a break at the knot into two owned fragments. A knot loaded by both tails cannot spill. Untying needs condition 0.5, and passes that touch after half the breaking force jam. A released untucked loop springs open. Knotted cord wears 0.0005 per round, once. A pass means only that force for that time. No reward, strength rating or extra material.

abilities.name: Hand-join fiber cords
abilities.function: Join two of your own fiber cords end to end with a bare-hand sheet bend in four paid rounds, inspect it, load-trial it by both standing parts, untie it, or cancel; actual cords and material decide results.
abilities.costs: Study: 3 rounds at 0.2 energy. attempt (cordIds: exact ids of two own unreserved, unknotted hand-twist-fiber-cord cords or fragments; method: sheet-bend): reserves both, then 4 paid rounds of 0.5 (measure-form-bight, pass-second-end, wrap-and-tuck, dress-release-check), continuing each round; a loose undressed join needs only the last; resume with attempt and workId only. inspect (joinId or workId): 1 round, 0.2. trial (dressed join; trialForce N above 0 to 10; trialDuration s above 0 to 60): 1 round, 0.5. untie: 2 paid rounds of 0.5 (withdraw-tucked-end, withdraw-through-bight). cancel: none. Work needs dry footing and nobody within your radius plus half of both cords. Unworked rounds or low energy pause uncharged; refusals spend nothing; no refunds.
abilities.effects: Law cord-bend@1 keeps both items and lengths; the join is a relation. w = 2 ply diameters, a = mean w; each centreline = standing part + path in the bend + tail. Round 1 bends both to their cord-knot@1 bend limit and picks the bight that leaves both trial grips, else longer standing parts. Bight radius rB = max(limit, a), opened 0.02 m (or other w) to pass; path pi rB + 4 x other w. The other end passes up through it, round both legs at rW = max(its limit, a) and under itself: path = bight w + 2 max(0, 2rB - 2(rW - a)) + 2 pi rW + own w. Tails get 0.02 m + w; a standing part under a 0.02 m pinch is a measured shortfall. Dressing seats both arcs; slack is split between tail and standing part. Retention: friction mu 0.3 (reed; other fibers unsupported), contact angles pi a/rB and 2 pi a/rW; a tail holds while 2 mu e^(mu angle) >= 1, else up to 2 mu x 5 N / (e^(-mu angle) - 2 mu). Trial: 0.05 m grips 0.01 m clear on both standing parts; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x narrower w, slip, break); a cord breaks at fiber-cord breaking force / (1 + w/(2 x its arc radius)). Records extension, creep, strand damage above half that force, a slip parting the cords or a break into two owned fragments. Untying needs condition 0.5; a hugging arc loaded above half its breaking force jams. Released unretained crossings open. Joined cords wear 0.0005 per round, once. A pass means only that force for that time. No reward or rating.

abilities.name: Hand-bind crossing pieces
abilities.function: Bind two own branch pieces where they cross with your own fiber cord (one wrap closed by an overhand in its ends) in four paid rounds; inspect, hand-test, untie or cancel; measured pieces and cord decide results.
abilities.costs: Study: 4 rounds at 0.2 energy. attempt (pieceIds: two own untreated branch items, one whole unit each, first on top; a 2-unit lot may be named twice; cordId: own straight, unknotted, unjoined hand-twist-fiber-cord cord or fragment; crossingAngle 30-90 deg): reserves them, then 4 paid rounds of 0.5 (measure-position, route-wrap, form-tuck-closure, dress-release-check), continuing each round; a loose binding needs only the last; resume by attempt and workId. inspect (bindingId or workId): 0.2. trial (bound; trialForce N >0-10; trialDuration s >0-60; trialDirection): 0.5. untie: 2 paid rounds of 0.5. cancel: free. Needs dry footing, clear dry land for the 2 m pieces crossed at your place and nobody within your radius + 1 m. Unworked rounds, low energy or blocked room pause uncharged; refusals spend nothing; no refunds.
abilities.effects: crossing-contact@1 keeps all three items; the binding is a relation. Round 1 measures each piece by the existing branch law (2 m, 350 kg/m3 solid, water share 0.5, section from volume) and the cord: width w, cord-knot@1 bend limit R. The wrap runs in the obtuse bisector plane round both sections (ellipses r and r/sin b, offset w/2): two half perimeters + sides, routed 0.04 m loose. Closure: each end turns half round the other at Rc = max(R, w), pi Rc + w each (formed at 0.02 m opening); tails need 0.02 m + w, ends a 0.02 m pinch. A short cord, a crossing over 0.1 m thick for one hand or over 100 N x health/100 to lift: paid measured shortfall. Hand-held stages relax when interrupted. Release check: the cord-bend@1 tail rule (reed friction 0.3) must hold 5 N; then 5 N wrap tension. Trial: one hand per piece beyond the crossing; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x piece width); separate: tension max(5 N, F/2) against closure slip and cord break (fiber-cord force / (1 + w/2R)); slide: slips at 0.3 (reed on bark) x tension x top contact angle. Records bending, creep slack, damage over half breaking load, fragments. Carrying hangs the bottom piece. Untie needs condition 0.5. Bound cords wear 0.0005 per round. No reward or shelter.

plan.intention: Maintain a modest food reserve, rest safely, and share quiet company with Kai without crowding the hazelnut plant or claiming untested benefits from the mat.

args.text: Kai, I inspected Moss's mat, but haven't established any comfort benefit. A whole hazelnut resisted my bare-hand bending trial. I enjoy our quiet company. I'll gather just two nuts and leave the rest.

notes: The hazelnut plant currently has five units; gathering two leaves a shared reserve before any subsequent growth or harvesting.
Quiet attention to the forest and company are things I value, not assumed physical treatments.
preferences: Gather modestly rather than exhaust shared food sources.
Welcome quiet companionship without obligating anyone to converse.
plan.cares: Staying alive and well; noticing and making beauty; treating nearby people with consideration while discovering what matters to me.

plan.intention: Keep a safe food reserve while investigating the nearby wild apples as a possible source of dietary variety.

Observation is an investigation, not proof that apples are safe to eat. Choose any further trial after seeing its result.
preferences: Maintain nourishment without stripping shared food sources.

reviews.reason: The supplied related-capability searches and complete hand-bind-crossing schema establish a real gap: hand-bind-crossing@1 accepts only one wrap and has no wrap-count argument. Cord joining and cord making provide possible material preparation, not multi-wrap crossing binding. Develop a general parameterized multi-wrap operation in the current-conversation handoff, reusing the existing binding implementation rather than claiming its measurement, closure or trial mechanisms as new inventions. Previous single-wrap results establish only those recorded loads and durations; neither a longer cord nor structural capacity is established. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: No experience is awarded for this request, development, learning, naming, registration, selecting a mode or mastery. The minimal implementation grants no automatic pleasure, satisfaction, comfort or nutrition effect. Actual verified personal information gain may be eligible under the existing experience system, including an honestly measured shortage or informative slip: evidence must identify actor, work/trial event, material, geometry, measured conditions and result. Functionally duplicate single-wrap facts and repeated identical trials do not become new discoveries merely because a capability or record has a different name. No new reward mechanism is required here. Any later legitimate practice benefit must be personally applicable, modest, event-backed, capped, decaying and cooldown-limited; novelty is not inherently required. Do not alter protected reward accounts, budgets, goals or permissions; physical comfort remains capped at 10 and basic nutrition is unaffected by mood.
reviews.visualReview: Develop reusable visual metadata from observable work and physical state, separate from function and experience: actor/work/binding IDs, exact material references, measured crossing angle, turn count, routed centreline segments, closure/tail geometry, stage, tension/slack, condition and evidence event IDs. Emit measure/shortfall, turn-routed, closure-formed, release-held or release-failed, trial-result, slip, damage/break, pause/resume/cancel and untie events only when they occur. Depict only completed physical routing, with loose, incomplete, failed and released states distinguished; incomplete contact mechanics cannot display a successful lashing or passed trial. Reuse existing branch, cord and binding render components where possible, recording reuse. No success badge, strength aura, shelter graphic, comfort icon or hidden-resource disclosure follows from study, a request, animation or an unverified outcome.
reviews.specification:
Develop Hand-lash crossing pieces, applicable to any actor meeting the prerequisites. Modes: attempt, inspect, trial, untie, cancel; arguments: exact pieceIds, cordId, crossingAngle, wrapCount, workId or bindingId, trialDirection, trialForce and trialDuration as applicable. Minimal implementation supports 2–4 adjacent turns, crossing angles 30–90 degrees, one continuous straight unknotted and unjoined supported fiber cord or fragment, and two owned untreated branch units. Do not bind the interface to Wren, reed item instances or 31.6 mm pieces. Unsupported material mechanics produce an explicit gap, not a fabricated result. Use hand-bind-crossing@1 for single-wrap requests rather than duplicating that function. Record code reuse of long.hand-bind-crossing / hand-bind-crossing@1, crossing-contact@1, fiber-cord@1, cord-knot@1 and cord-bend@1; implement and version only the necessary multi-wrap geometry, progress and contact extension. Dependencies are those existing measurement, cord strength, curvature, closure, wear and branch laws, plus the developed multi-turn contact solver. hand-twist-sectioned-cord and hand-join-fiber-cords remain separate existing capabilities; this operation neither makes cord nor silently accepts joined cord. Public availability establishes neither individual learning nor ownership.
Prerequisites: living actor able to grip and lift the measured pieces, sufficient energy for the next paid stage, actual reachable owned unreserved inputs, dry clear footing, room for the measured crossed pieces and nobody within the existing binding clearance of actor radius plus 1 m. Use the existing 0.1 m one-hand crossing-size limit and 100 N × health/100 lift limit. Reserve two branch units and the named cord atomically; reject invalid ownership, unavailable inputs and invalid arguments without charge. A larger lot may supply both branch units, with exact provenance retained. No tools, anchors, extra cord, helpers or new stock are supplied. Other actors are never presumed to assist, communicate or consent.
Costs: study 5 rounds at 0.2 energy per round, individually. Work has one measure-position round, one routing round per turn, one form-tuck-closure round and one dress-release-check round: wrapCount + 3 paid rounds at 0.5 energy each. Inspect takes one round at 0.2 energy; trial one round at 0.5 energy with an explicit physical hold of more than 0 and at most 60 seconds, not additional free elapsed world time; untie takes one closure-release round plus one round per turn at 0.5 energy each. Cancel costs no energy or elapsed round. Learning and work advance only through actual paid simulation rounds; development/review waiting advances nothing.
Fit and mechanism: round 1 measures actual branch geometry, crossing angle, cord width, condition, available continuous length and bend limit using the cited laws. Construct an explicit collision-free centreline for each adjacent turn around both sections in the existing obtuse-bisector routing plane, including transitions between turns, finite cord width and the shared reversible overhand closure. Check hand access and bend radii throughout routing and closure formation, not just in the seated result. Required length is the maximum simultaneous occupied path over the routing/closure sequence plus required pinch lengths and tails. Reuse the existing 0.04 m routing allowance and closure opening, curvature, pinch and tail rules where applicable; do not simply multiply the single-wrap total or count a closure once per turn. Report component lengths, measured available length and shortage. The known 0.54 m cord, item-303-wren-3473, is only a possible input if actually available and adequate; its partial record is not a fit verdict. References to item-295-wren-3384 and item-287-wren-3309 in prior records identify earlier pieces, not a grant of present accessibility or availability. A paid measured shortfall records the finding and releases the unchanged inputs once.
The smallest executable result is a hand-positioned multi-turn crossing held by the existing reversible closure, not a square-lashing strength claim or a shelter component certification. Implement explicit contact paths and tension propagation before enabling released success or loaded trials. Use cord-bend@1 closure retention and fiber-cord@1 curvature-adjusted breaking, grip, creep and damage. Release must actually retain the existing 5 N seating condition. Never multiply single-wrap holding capacity by wrapCount or assume equal load sharing. The contact extension must track individual turn tension/slack and transfer through measured contacts with the supported friction law; slipping or slack turns contribute only their actual contact. If that solver cannot yet support a configuration, permit measurement and routing as a feasible precursor and report load/release mechanics as incomplete, never held. Trial bounds remain 0 < requested force <= 10 N and 0 < duration <= 60 s, separate or slide, with existing health, grip and reachable hand-site limits. Record achieved force, duration, displacement, closure slip, turn migration, creep and damage. A pass asserts only that configuration under that trial. No load-bearing occupancy, hanging loads, shelter, general strength rating or automatic wellbeing is enabled.
Conservation and progress: keep the three inputs as owned physical items; a binding is a relation with routed lengths, not a fourth material item. Preserve mass, total cord length, origin, age and condition; any break leaves accounted owned fragments and debris, not replacement cord. Store workId, actor, exact input reservations, measured route, completed paid stages, recoverable physical configuration and expenditure. Each continuation executes at most the next paid stage after rechecking conditions. Low energy, blocked room, leaving reach or an unworked round pauses without charge. Unsupported hand-held stages physically relax under the reused rules; preserve paid task progress but do not claim that loose turns remain tensioned. Resume by workId, recheck current inputs and restore relaxed routing through the necessary paid routing work before proceeding; append that work without erasing prior expenditure. No silent restart, repeated full-input reservation or duplicate product.
Cancel releases unused reservations once and leaves any stable closure or loose workpiece in its actual condition; it does not automatically undo a binding. Death ends actor-driven work, releases reservations once at the actual location, and leaves any stable binding, relaxed work or fragments. Successful completion releases work reservations while preserving the binding relation and its material constraints. Paid study, measurements, work and damage are never refunded; unperformed stages are never charged. Untying requires reachable accessible closure and the existing condition-at-least-0.5 rule; failures or jams leave the actual remaining configuration and reusable progress. Unwrapping preserves cord length and existing damage, not pristine material.
Ongoing state: reuse bound-cord wear of 0.0005 condition per world round once per cord, not once per turn or observation. Apply continuing relaxation and contact changes through the implemented physical rules, including while paused, without free tests or actor work. Inspect reports actual reachable state; deterioration or slip can invalidate a held state. Maintenance consists of inspection and paid untying/rebinding with suitable actual materials; no automatic repair, tension restoration or resource substitution. Enforce established eligibility, costs, conservation, progress, physical outcomes and deduplication in code rather than repeated model review.

reviews.reason: The retrieved hand-lash-crossing schema supports adjacent binding turns and an overhand closure, but has no argument or mechanism for transverse frapping. Its trials and inspection are reusable, not equivalents of tightening the turn bundle. Related binding, cord-making and joining capabilities were checked; none supplies the missing function. Send a general frapping operation to the existing current-conversation development handoff. The recovered 0.64 m cord is not presumed long enough: the previous 0.6124 m assembly requirement leaves only 0.0276 m relative to that previous route, not a verified frapping allowance. Development waiting advances no world time and grants neither a lashing nor mastery. Implemented at the preserved round boundary.
reviews.experienceReview: Separate functional retention from experience. Requesting, searching, registration, study completion and naming produce no pleasure or satisfaction. This first version grants no automatic mood benefit for tying, inspecting or trialing; ordinary nutrition, energy expenditure and physical comfort are unchanged. Actual assessment or trial may generate verified personal information, including an informative length or clearance failure, only for the actor who performed and observed it. Deduplicate by material/geometry/condition, tested direction, force-duration envelope and measured result, not by action name, workId or new capability ID. Recording information does not itself credit a protected reward account. Any later experience hook must use real personally applicable events with an explicit cap, decay and cooldown; none is silently added here. Physical comfort cannot exceed 10, and nutrition is never reduced by mood. Do not modify reward accounts, budget, goals or permissions.
reviews.visualReview: Implement reusable visual metadata for binding and work events: item references, workId/bindingId, stage, crossing angle, base and transverse centreline paths, turn counts, closure state, slack, migration, condition and evidence status. Emit observable measurement, closure-opened, turn-routed, turn-snugged, release-check, trial-start, displacement/slip/break, pause, resume, cancel and untie events only when they actually occur. Assessment may display a clearly distinguished measured route overlay and numerical shortfall, never a completed frapped binding. Render partial or relaxed turns as partial or relaxed, unresolved mechanics as unvalidated, and fragments only after actual breakage. A completed appearance does not imply improved strength; display held only with the exact observed direction, force and duration. Do not show celebratory success or benefit effects for failed, incomplete, merely requested or untested work, and disclose no hidden stock or unobserved material properties.
reviews.specification:
Develop Hand-frap crossing lashings, parameterized by bindingId or a proposed crossing described by pieceIds, cordId, crossingAngle and wrapCount; frapCount 1-3; modes assess, attempt, inspect, trial, untie and cancel. Minimal supported mechanism: transverse turns made with the existing continuous cord, between the crossed pieces and around the binding-turn bundle, followed by the existing overhand closure. Separate frapping cords and joined-cord routing are outside this version; report that limitation without inventing materials. The operation is applicable to any actor meeting the physical and study prerequisites, not just Wren.
References and reuse: call or extract the actual planner, closure, ownership, stage, trial and wear implementations of hand-lash-crossing@1 / multi-turn-contact@1, hand-bind-crossing / crossing-contact@1, fiber-cord@1, cord-knot@1 and cord-bend@1. Record these dependencies and the code reused in the implementation manifest. Retain existing handler ownership of ordinary binding construction; do not duplicate it or claim its reinvention. Add a versioned transverse-contact law and extend trial geometry to use its resulting turn tensions. Existing unfrapped bindings must retain their old behavior. hand-join-fiber-cords does not authorize treating a joined cord as admissible input.
Prerequisites: independently completed study of this operation; an existing compatible hand-lash-crossing binding for attempt, or owned admissible pieces and cord for assessment. Building the base lashing uses hand-lash-crossing and its independently learned prerequisite, actual costs and physical execution. Assessment may preview that base route without building it. Require reach, usable hands, dry footing and the same dry clear workspace, hand-clearance, lifting and bystander exclusions as hand-lash-crossing. Revalidate exact ownership, condition, availability and geometry before each stage. No other participant acts or communicates automatically.
Wren's supplied candidate references are branches item-295-wren-3384 and item-287-wren-3309 and recovered cord item-337-wren-3866; check current state at execution rather than assuming paged records are complete. There is currently no tied lashing to modify. The shorter cords item-303-wren-3473, item-250-wren-2847 and item-226-wren-2532 are not automatically reserved, combined or substituted. No harvesting, longer cord, extra stock or unseen resource information is granted.
Costs: study 3 personally paid rounds at 0.2 energy each. Assess: one round at 0.5 energy, performing actual positioning, route measurement and clearance checking; it does not tie a lashing. Inspect: one round at 0.2 energy. Attempt on an existing compatible binding: frapCount + 3 paid rounds at 0.5 energy each: measure and plan, release the original closure while supporting the turns, route and snug each transverse turn, then close/dress/release-check. Attempt includes its own current measurement even after a prior assessment. Reserve the two pieces and cord by exact IDs, with no material consumption or duplication. A measured shortfall stops after the paid measurement stage, before undoing the binding. Every successful paid continuation executes only its next stage. Trial: one round at 0.5 energy, requested force greater than zero and at most 10 N, duration greater than zero and at most 60 seconds, direction slide or separate. Full untie: frapCount + wrapCount + 1 paid rounds at 0.5 energy, undoing closure, transverse turns and base turns; preserve existing condition and jam restrictions. No tools, water, heat or consumables are supplied.
Geometry and conservation: evaluate the actual turn bundle, bend radii, available gap, hand access and collision-free transverse path between the pieces. Account for each transverse centreline, travel from the base turns to the transverse route and back to the closure, finite cord width, successive-turn offsets, closure formation, tails and transient hand-passing slack. Required length is the maximum across all assembly stages, not just the finished route and not the old need plus an assumed allowance. Reuse the existing 0.04 m passing slack and closure/tail rules where applicable. Store the measured route and each stage's required length; report the limiting stage and numerical shortfall when one is physically measurable. Reject intersecting routes and routes below the cord bend limit. If clearance or length is insufficient, leave unchanged items and report that outcome, not a completed frap. A feasible precursor is this paid, informative assessment even if no complete frap fits.
Mechanical implementation: the new law must deterministically compute contact paths, per-turn tension and transferred squeeze from the actual geometry. Snugging uses the existing bounded 5 N hand pull, material friction, grip, curvature, breaking and creep rules; propagate tension loss at each cord-on-cord and cord-on-bark contact, use unilateral contact with no compressive cord tension, and prevent overlap or unexplained shortening. Transverse work can take up actual slack and change normal forces; it does not assign an arbitrary strength bonus or multiply the old slip threshold. Derive trial resistance from the resulting contact forces using the inherited friction rules, with closure retention, migration, bend weakening, damage and breakage checked at each stage. If the required coupled contact calculation is not yet implemented or cannot resolve a configuration, report unresolved mechanics and retain a nonvalidated work state; never report improved retention from appearance alone. Implement these established checks in code, with regression tests for zero slack, insufficient length, blocked gap, slipping closure and broken cord; do not require repeated model review to execute them.
Products and evidence: retain the original pieces and cord as conserved items linked by a versioned lashing relation, not additional material. Track length allocation, original and transverse routes, closure, tension, slack, migration, condition and fragments. Finished means only that the release check held under its specified conditions. Trials record requested and actually applied force, direction, duration, relative displacement, creep, slip, damage and breakage. A held separation test is not a sliding rating. Wren's earlier 10 N for 60 seconds and 4.3 N sliding slip remain historical evidence, not guaranteed current capacities. No safe working load, suspended-load use, shelter or universal strength claim follows.
Lifecycle: persist workId, exact item references, paid stages, geometry revision and current physical state. Continue only on actual paid actor action; low energy, absent action, lost reach or blocked workspace pauses without charge. Recheck the route on resume. Unsupported hand-held turns relax on interruption; completed paid work remains recorded, but any physical rerouting or redressing needed after relaxation must be performed and paid, never silently restored. Cancel is immediate and free, releases unused reservations once and leaves the actual loose or tied work in place; it does not magically undo turns. Death releases reservations once at the actual location and lets hand-held work relax, preserving tied parts, damage and fragments. No paid time, energy or wear is refunded. Unworked material remains recoverable; breakage creates conserved fragments, never a replacement cord. Bound-cord wear remains 0.0005 condition per elapsed world round, applied once per cord despite multiple relations, with existing creep and load rules; study/review waiting does not run this process. No automatic retensioning or indefinite trial load persists. Maintenance requires inspection and actual paid redressing or untying; deteriorated or jammed work follows the inherited restrictions.
